sections.heading: How to Play Windwalker
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="How to Play Windwalker"][color=c10]Windwalker Monk Rotation in Midnight Season 2[/color][/h2]
Although Windwalker Monks have one of the most unique Masteries in the game, the spec's playstyle can be simplified into a few important things to remember. The core concepts to keep in mind are these:

[wrapper width=1100px][box border=true]
[center][table style=grid]
[tr][td]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=trade_alchemy_potionb3 size=medium type=round color=c10 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c10]Don't Repeat Abilities:[/color][/b] Don't hit the same ability twice in a row. Midnight added a new buff that tracks what button you pressed last, track that buff using the in-game options or another tool.
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=ability_monk_energizingwine size=medium type=round color=c10 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c10]Avoid Overcapping Resources:[/color][/b] Windwalker has to manage both Energy and Chi, try to avoid wasting them. There are times where wasting resources cannot be avoided, but as a general rule, try to do this as little as possible.
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=ability_monk_risingsunkick size=medium type=round color=c10 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c10]Use Abilities with Cooldowns:[/color][/b] Abilities with short cooldowns like [spell=107428] and [spell=113656] are some of the most important damage abilities you have. Avoid abilities with cooldowns sitting unused as this often leaves to lost damage potential.
        [/td]
	[/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=inv_ability_monk_weaponsoforder size=medium type=round color=c10 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c10]Plan your [spell=1249625] Usage:[/color][/b] [spell=1249625] has a very flexible cooldown depending on your choice of talents, plan when to use it to maximize its strength.  [spell=1249625] can be a 60, 70, 80, or a 90-second cooldown, you'll likely want to go with a 60-second or 90-second cooldown and adjust for using it every 60, 90, or 120 seconds depending on the fight.
        [/td]
	[/tr]
[/table]
[/td][/tr][/table]
[/center]
[/box][/wrapper]
[pad]
[center][cta-button guide=32794 icon=spell_monk_windwalker_spec]Windwalker Monk Starter Guide[/cta-button][/center]

sections.heading: Rotation Priority
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="Rotation Priority"][icon name=spell_monk_windwalker_spec type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon] Best Windwalker Monk Rotation[/h2]
For all forms of content, Windwalker follows a priority list of what spells to cast. Your goal should be to cast the highest priority abilities as often as you can, while managing the resources that are required to do so, and not pressing the same ability twice in a row.

Below, we break down the main priority lists for Windwalker Monk: Single-Target Rotation, AoE Rotation, and your opener sequence.
[wrapper width=70%][center][box border=true]
	[center][large][b][color=white]Hero Talent Master Switches[/color][/b][/large]
	[pad]
	You can use the master switches below to flip the [b][i]entire page's[/i][/b] options to your selected choice.[/center]
	[center]
	[wrapper width=95%]
		[grid width=99%]
			[display-option="shado-pan" radio="Hero" icon=inv_ability_shadopanmonk_flurrystrikes checked] Shado Pan[/display-option]
			[display-option="conduit-of-the-celestials" radio="Hero" icon=inv_ability_conduitofthecelestialsmonk_celestialconduit] Conduit of the Celestials[/display-option]
		[/grid]
	[/wrapper]
	[/center]
[/box][/center][/wrapper]
[br]
[tabs name="Rotations" uniform=true]

[tab name="Single-Target Priority" icon=spell_holy_divinespirit]
	[h3 toc="Single Target Priority" type=bar][color=c10] Best Windwalker Monk Single Target Rotation[/color][/h3]
	[pad]
Windwalker in Single Target plays around a priority list, juggling both ability cooldowns and resources based on an order of power. This means with each GCD we go top to bottom on a list, and press the button with the current highest value.

[span display-options="!(shado-pan)&!(conduit-of-the-celestials)"]As both [b][symbol=wow-hero-talent-shado-pan] [color=#FFAD36]Shado-pan[/color][/b] and [b][symbol=wow-hero-talent-conduit-of-the-celestials] [color=#67ECAF]Conduit of the Celestials[/color][/b] have an impact on your priority, you can use the buttons below to switch between each [b]Hero Talent[/b].[/span][span display-options="shado-pan"]With [b][symbol=wow-hero-talent-shado-pan] [color=#FFAD36]Shado-pan[/color][/b] selected, the priority is as follows:[/span][span display-options="conduit-of-the-celestials"]With [b][symbol=wow-hero-talent-conduit-of-the-celestials] [color=#67ECAF]Conduit of the Celestials[/color][/b] selected, the priority is as follows:[/span]


	[div display-options="!(shado-pan)&!(conduit-of-the-celestials)"]
	[center][box border=true]
	[b][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-legendary-available] Please select a Hero Talent option to generate a Single Target priority[/b]
	[/box][/center]
	[/div]

[wrapper width=850px]
	[div display-options="shado-pan"]
	[wrapper][center][box border=true][center][small][i]The builds used below are covered in the [url guide=3280]Talents page[/url]. Anywhere you see the [span class=tip tooltip=NotesHighlight][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span] icon, you can hover over it for additional notes.[/i][/small][/center]
	[/box][/center]
	[/wrapper]
[br]
[b][symbol=wow-hero-talent-shado-pan] [color=#FFAD36]Shado-pan[/color][/b] focuses most of its damage in an even spread of most abilities. With the changes in Midnight, many of the extra things that you used to have to track, like Energy consumption and stacks of various buffs are gone and things are much simpler and easier to manage.

Anywhere you see the [span class=tip tooltip=NotesHighlight][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span] icon, you can hover over it for additional notes.[/i][/small][/center]

[br]
[b][symbol=wow-hero-talent-conduit-of-the-celestials] [color=#67ECAF]Conduit of the Celestials[/color][/b] is focused on managing the additional cooldown of [spell=443028] and the effects from [spell=443294]. This burst window accelerates how quickly your abilities come off cooldown and how quickly you channel [spell=113656] allow you to squeeze a large amount of damage into its buff window.

[tab name="AoE Priority" icon=spell_holy_prayerofspirit]
	[h3 toc="AoE Priority" type=bar][color=c10] Best Windwalker Monk AoE  Rotation[/color][/h3]
	[pad]
With current tuning, Windwalker AOE differs very little compared to how it functions in single target. We shift to a multi-target priority at [b]2 targets[/b], and both Hero Trees differ significantly on [i]where[/i] damage comes from.

	[span display-options="shado-pan"] With [symbol=wow-hero-talent-shado-pan] [color=#FFAD36]Shado-pan[/color] selected, the priority is as follows:[/span][span display-options="conduit-of-the-celestials"] With [symbol=wow-hero-talent-conduit-of-the-celestials] [color=#67ECAF]Conduit of the Celestials[/color] selected, the priority is as follows:[/span]

[tab name="Opener" icon=ability_vehicle_launchplayer]
[h3 toc="Opener" type=bar][color=c10] Best Windwalker Monk Opener[/color][/h3]
	[pad]
The Windwalker Monk opener is somewhat affected by your choice of Hero Talents. [symbol=wow-hero-talent-conduit-of-the-celestials] [color=#67ECAF]Conduit of the Celestials[/color] looks to follow a relatively prescribed sequence, whereas [symbol=wow-hero-talent-shado-pan] [color=#FFAD36]Shado-pan[/color]'s opener generally mirrors the priority and looks to get the important abilities on cooldown as quickly as you can so that you can get them back sooner.

[span display-options="!(shado-pan)&!(conduit-of-the-celestials)"]You can use the buttons below to display openers for both single-target and AoE, depending on your chosen [b]Hero Talent[/b].[/span][span display-options="shado-pan"]With [symbol=wow-hero-talent-shado-pan] [color=#FFAD36]Shado-pan[/color] selected, opener details are as follows:[/span][span display-options="conduit-of-the-celestials"]With [symbol=wow-hero-talent-conduit-of-the-celestials] [color=#67ECAF]Conduit of the Celestials[/color] selected, opener details are as follows:[/span]

	[wrapper width=850px]
	[div display-options="!(shado-pan)&!(conduit-of-the-celestials)"]
	[center]
	[box border=true]
	[b][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-legendary-available] Please select a Hero Talent option to generate an Opener sequence[/b]
	[/box]
	[/center]
	[/div]
	[/wrapper]
	[wrapper][center][box border=true][center][small][i]The builds used below are covered in the [url guide=3280]Talents page[/url]. Anywhere you see the [span class=tip tooltip=NotesHighlight][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span] icon, you can hover over it for additional notes.[/i][/small][/center]
	[/box][/center]
	[/wrapper]
[br]
The [symbol=wow-hero-talent-shado-pan] [color=#FFAD36]Shado-pan[/color] opener aims to get stronger abilities like [spell=113656] and [spell=107428] on cooldown as quickly as possible so that you can use it more often. Generally, the opener follows the priority closer than openers often do. [b]The opener is also the same for single target and AOE.[/b]

[h3 toc=false type=bar][color=c10]Sample Timeline[/color][/h3]
[pad]

sections.heading: Major Cooldowns
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Major Cooldowns" type=bar][color=c10][icon name=spell_monk_windwalker_spec type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon] Windwalker Monk Major Cooldowns[/color][/h2]
Windwalker has access to a few abilities that count as longer cooldowns and not just rotational abilities. All of them come with some extra wrinkles in how they work rather than simply being flat increases, so the below section covers [i]how[/i] they work, and most importantly, how to get the most out of each use.

[pad]
[tabs name="cds" uniform=true iconborders=true]

[tab name="Zenith" icon=inv_ability_monk_weaponsoforder]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=inv_ability_monk_weaponsoforder type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon][color=monk] Zenith\u200e [/color][/h3]
[spell=1249625] doesn't provide any direct damage increase without the addition of additional talents like the Apex Talents of [spell=1261703]. However, it does reduce the cost of all of your Chi spenders by 1 and increases the cooldown reduction provided by [spell=100784] by an additional second. When you press the button it resets the cooldown of [spell=107428] and provides you an additional 2 Chi to use right away.

Key takeaways are:
[ul]
[li]While [spell=1249625] is active, [spell=100784] becomes free, so it is your primary filler in order to get [spell=107428] and [spell=113656] back from cooldown as quickly as possible.
[ul]
[li icon=angle-double-right]This also means that you can very quickly feel like you have too much Chi if you're also using [spell=100780] too often.[/li]
[/ul]
[/li]
[li]Due to getting your cooldowns back faster, it is even more important to have the Chi that you need to cast them right away.[/li]
[li]If talented into [spell=1249832] then [spell=100784] generates a Chi rather than consuming one. This causes it to function as both your primary filler and primary Chi-builder.[/li]
[ul]
[li icon=angle-double-right][spell=100780] can be used in between [spell=100784]s to add a stack of [spell=116645] for the ensuing [spell=100784]. This can result in overcapping your Chi at times, but this is preferable to casting nothing.[/li]
[/ul]
[li][spell=1249625] has two stacks, so you do not need to use it as soon as it is available but can plan its use for the best possible time.[/li]
[ul]
[li icon=angle-double-right]Through talents, [spell=1249625] can have a cooldown that takes 60, 70, 80, or 90-seconds to return. With two possible stacks, this means you can safely use it based on when you get the most value out of it, during a high-damage phase of a fight, a time with many targets to hit, or during large buffs like [spell=2825] or with your trinkets.[/li]
[/ul]
[/ul]

[ul]--------------- Commented Out to add back when Apex Talents are usable ---------------

[minor-heading type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_monk_tigereyebrandy type=round size=small inline=true color=c1][/icon] [color=warrior]Tigereye Brew[/color][/minor-heading]

TEB's stacking mechanic is stupid and makes you think about some dumb shit, here's where you read all about the dumb shit you have to think about.

--------------- Commented Out to add back when Apex Talents are usable ---------------[/ul]

[pad]
[/tab]

[tab name="Celestial Conduit" icon=inv_ability_conduitofthecelestialsmonk_celestialconduit]

[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=inv_ability_conduitofthecelestialsmonk_celestialconduit type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon][color=monk] Celestial Conduit[/color][/h3]
[spell=443028] is a powerful ability to use, but the most powerful aspect of it is that it adds the [spell=443294] buff. However, because this buff can also come from using [spell=392983] or [spell=152175], you need to stagger these uses for maximum benefit. This generally means using [spell=443028] spaced out between casts of [spell=392983] or [spell=152175]. This attempts to insure maximum uptime and value.

The instance of [spell=443294] that is triggered from using [spell=1249625] stacks with the version of [spell=443294] that comes from [spell=443028], [spell=392983], or [spell=152175]. However, the instance of [spell=443294] that is generated from [spell=443028] does not stack with the instance that comes from [spell=392983] or [spell=152175].

This means that you can cast [spell=1249625] when you already have [spell=443294] up, and you should because they stack very well. You want to try and avoid casting [spell=443028] if you already have the buff that comes from [spell=392983] or [spell=152175] and visa versa.

Key takeaways are:
[ul]
[li]Try to cast [spell=1249625] during [spell=443294].[/li]
[li]Try NOT to cast [spell=443028] if you still have the [spell=443294] buff from [spell=392983] or [spell=152175].[/li]
[li]Try NOT to cast [spell=392983] or [spell=152175] if you have the  [spell=443294] buff from [spell=443028].[/li]
[/ul]

[pad]
[/tab]

[tab name="Invoke Xuen" icon=ability_monk_summontigerstatue]

[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_monk_summontigerstatue type=round size=medium inline=true color=c8][/icon] [color=mage]Invoke Xuen[/color][/h3]

With the changes in Midnight [spell=123904] is mainly a button you press so that you can then channel [spell=443028] afterwards. This means that you'll want to plan ahead slightly so that you are not wasting a GCD summoning Xuen when you want to be dealing damage.

There is a large window after casting [spell=123904] where you're able to cast [spell=443028]. Because balancing the above [spell=443294] buff generally means a somewhat strict sequence of abilities, you will want to avoid deviating much from the above opener, even if it's the middle of a fight.


[pad]
[/tab]

[tab name="Touch of Death" icon=ability_monk_touchofdeath]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_monk_touchofdeath type=round size=medium inline=true color=red][/icon][color=red] Touch of Death[/color][/h3]

[spell=322109] seems like a straightforward ability to use but attempting to min/max it can lead to losing damage rather than gaining it. With the change to [spell=394123] in Midnight, it no longer provides a damage increase after using it.

While this generally means that you'll want to use it as soon as its available and you have space to press it without delaying another ability, it also means that you CAN try to use it right before the target dies  when your target has less health than your maximum health so that it deals 100% of your health rather than just the 35% of your maximum health that it deals if you use it on a target that is at 15% health or lower.

This is a very small window and [spell=322109] can sometimes have a delay before being usable if you just swap to a target to try and hit it with [spell=322109]. This delay can be the difference between making or missing the very small window. Missing the window generally means that you don't get [spell=322109] off and thus lose damage that you would have done if you had cast it sooner.

[pad]
[/tab]

[tab name="Touch of Karma" icon=ability_monk_touchofkarma]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_monk_touchofkarma type=round size=medium inline=true color=c8][/icon][color=mage] Touch of Karma[/color][/h3]
[spell=122470] is, first and foremost, a defensive ability. Its primary use is to absorb some damage in order to lessen the damage that you are dealt. However, the secondary function of [spell=122470] is that some of the damage that the shield absorbs is redirected back to the target that you cast the spell on. This means that [spell=122470] can be used offensively if you do not need its defensive value.

Most fights in most content have times where you will be taking damage and can cleanly use [spell=122470] for both its defensive and offensive value. However, sometimes the damage you are taking isn't enough to necessitate a defensive cooldown like [spell=122470]. In these situations it is, technically, optimal to find some damage that you can then absorb and redirect. This can be done through standing in some damage effect on the ground, or in extreme situations, casting [spell=115546] on a target and taking a few smacks.

Needing to [spell=115546] a target to get the benefit from [spell=122470] should be used as a last resort and only ever be done with the express permission of your tanks and healers as you're often likely to get killed once the shield ends without direct intervention. [b]Do this at your own risk.[/b]


[pad]
[/tab]

[tab name="Fortifying Brew" icon=ability_monk_fortifyingale_new]
[minor-heading type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_monk_fortifyingale_new type=round size=medium inline=true color=c4][/icon] [color=rogue]Fortifying Brew[/color][/minor-heading]

[spell=115203] increases your maximum health, so it also increases the damage that [spell=322109] deals and that [spell=122470] can absorb. Because of this, using [spell=115203] before you use [spell=322109] or [spell=122470] is a damage increase. This can be used to further improve your defense in a time of need, but it also has the secondary effect of increasing the amount of damage that is redirected back to the target.

If you are not going to need the defensive value of [spell=115203] on its own, like if large damage intake is more frequent and you need to stagger your defensive cooldowns, then you can stack them together for added benefit. Just be sure to use [spell=115203] BEFORE using  [spell=322109] or [spell=122470] as both snapshot on use.

A real good way to use this is to find a way to use [spell=115203] then [spell=122470] at a time when you'll also be able to use  [spell=322109] during the duration of [spell=115203]. This gets you both benefits for one use. If you're already going to use it for DPS purposes, then you might as well be efficient about it.

[pad]
[/tab]


[/tabs]
